chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Al-Khayrani, from his father, who said:
I was standing before Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام in Khurasan, when a man said to him: “O my master, if an occurrence were to happen, then to whom [would the matter go]?”
He said: “To Abū Jaʿfar, my son.”

Then it was as though the speaker considered the age of Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام too small, so Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام said: “Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent ʿĪsā ibn Maryam as a Messenger, a Prophet, and the bearer of an initiated law, at an age younger than the age in which Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام is.”

key_terms.أَبِي الْحَسَنِ: Abū al-Ḥasan, the Imam speaking in the narration
key_terms.أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ: Abū Jaʿfar, the son designated as successor
key_terms.اسْتَصْغَرَ: regarded as too small or belittled due to youth
key_terms.رَسُولًا: a messenger sent by Allah with divine mission
key_terms.شَرِيعَةٍ مُبْتَدَأَةٍ: a newly initiated law or revealed dispensation
key_terms.عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ: Jesus son of Mary, cited as an example of early divine appointment
key_terms.كَوْنٌ: an occurring event, here implying the Imam’s death or passing

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith show that Imam al-Jawad عليه السلام could hold divine authority despite his young age?
ai.summary: This hadith records a designation of Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام as successor by Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام. When the young age of Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام seemed surprising, the Imam responded by citing ʿĪsā ibn Maryam, whom Allah sent with prophethood and a new law at an even younger age, indicating that divine authority is not restricted by age.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Al Khayrani, from his father who said,
‘I had paused in front of Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> at Khurasan, so a speaker said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘O my Chief! If there was an occurrence (death), so to whom?’
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘To Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, my<sup>asws</sup> son<sup>asws</sup>’.

So it was as if the speaker was belittling the (young) age of Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>. So Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High Sent Isa<sup>as</sup> Ibn Maryam<sup>as</sup> as a Rasool<sup>as</sup>, a Prophet<sup>as</sup>, an owner of a Law, commencing during an age smaller than that which is in Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 13. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from al-Khayrani, from his father who has said the following.
“Once I was standing before abu al-Hassan (a.s.) in Khurasan and someone said tp him, “O my master, if something will happen to who (will go Leadership with Divine Authority)?”
The Imam (a.s.) said, “It will go to abu Ja‘far (a.s.), my son.”

The person asking the question thought of abu Ja‘far (a.s.) as very young for such task. Abu al-Hassan (a.s.) said, “Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, sent Jesus, son of Mary as a messenger prophet, the owner of a whole legal system. He began his task when he was smaller in age than abu Ja‘far (a.s.).”
